executiveSummary: Iteration 000038 implements the --yolo flag feature across all eight agent-invoking nvst commands. The implementation correctly threads `yolo: boolean` from CLI options through handler option interfaces to `invokeAgent`, and the agent dispatch logic in `src/agent.ts` correctly appends bypass args for Codex and Copilot in interactive mode when `yolo=true`. TypeScript typecheck passes with zero errors and all 213 tests pass. The only minor deviation is that the help-text description for `--yolo` reads "Suppress agent permission prompts" rather than the verbatim text specified in FR-1: "Invoke agent with bypass-permissions flags (suppresses agent permission prompts)". All functional behaviour is fully compliant.

verificationByFR.notes: All eight agent-invoking commands declare `.option("--yolo", ...)` as required, but the description string used is "Suppress agent permission prompts" instead of the specified "Invoke agent with bypass-permissions flags (suppresses agent permission prompts)". Behaviour is correct; only the help text wording differs.

`yolo: boolean` is present in every handler options interface (IdeateOptions, DefineRequirementOptions, RefineRequirementOptions, RefineProjectContextOptions, CreatePrototypeOptions, CreateProjectContextOptions, AuditPrototypeOptions, RefactorPrototypeOptions) and forwarded to invokeAgentFn at each call site.
`AgentInvokeOptions` in `src/agent.ts` line 20 declares `yolo?: boolean`. Default value of `false` is applied at destructuring in `invokeAgent`.

In `buildAgentArgs`: codex interactive branch appends `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` when yolo=true; copilot interactive branch appends `--yolo --no-ask-user` when yolo=true. Non-interactive paths are unaffected.
`--yolo` and `--force` are independent options on every command. They can be combined freely with no conflict.
No new runtime dependencies were introduced. Changes are pure TypeScript additions to existing files.

verificationByUS.notes: All seven acceptance criteria are satisfied: AC01 — --yolo present on all 8 commands (help text wording is minor); AC02 — yolo forwarded to invokeAgent in every handler; AC03 — yolo?: boolean optional in AgentInvokeOptions; AC04 — bypass args injected when yolo=true for codex and copilot interactive; AC05 — no bypass args added when yolo=false (non-interactive paths unchanged); AC06 — bun tsc --noEmit exits 0; AC07 — bun test exits 0 with 213 pass / 0 fail.

minorObservations: FR-1 specifies the exact help-text string: "Invoke agent with bypass-permissions flags (suppresses agent permission prompts)". The implementation uses the shorter: "Suppress agent permission prompts". While functionally equivalent, aligning the wording with the PRD is recommended for consistency.

Claude's interactive branch in `buildAgentArgs` always adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions` regardless of the yolo flag (line 113). The PRD scopes FR-4 to Codex and Copilot only, so this is not a violation, but it means Claude users cannot opt out of bypass permissions in interactive mode — worth documenting.
Gemini's interactive branch (line 102-103) does not have a yolo-conditional path. If Gemini gains an equivalent bypass flag in the future, the pattern would need to be extended.

The test file `tests/it_000038_us-001-yolo-flag.test.ts` covers AC01–AC05 thoroughly. AC06 and AC07 (typecheck and test pass) are validated implicitly by the CI/build pipeline rather than a dedicated test assertion, which is acceptable.
conclusionsAndRecommendations: The implementation is fully compliant with all functional requirements and the single user story. The only actionable item is a cosmetic fix to align the --yolo help-text description with the exact wording specified in FR-1. No regressions were introduced, all tests pass, and the codebase typechecks cleanly. Recommendation: apply the minor help-text fix in a fast follow-up (one-line change per command in src/cli.ts), then proceed to approve the prototype.
